voyage.name: Basilica di San Petronio
voyage.content: It had to be the largest church in the world and in the shape of a huge Latin cross, but was only completed the long arm and with the unfinished façade. The basilica is still one of the most beautiful examples of Italian Gothic style and is one of the greatest monuments in the city. The Basilica houses an invaluable number of treasures such as the sundial by Cassini and Guglielmini, which indicates the exact period o

voyage.name: Palazzo del Podestà
voyage.content: The first seat of the city government.

voyage.name: Palazzo Re Enzo
voyage.content: The palace was built between 1244-1246 as an extension of the nearby Palazzo del Podestà. It takes its name from Enzio of Sardinia, Frederick II's son, who was prisoner here from 1249 until his death in 1272. The current Gothic appearance dates from the restoration of 1905 due to Alfonso Rubbiani.

voyage.name: Fontana di Nettuno
voyage.content: A fountain built in 1563 by Tommaso Laureti of Palermo, later embellished by Jean de Boulogne (called Giambologna). It is considered to be one of Bologna’s symbols, and renovated in 2017.

voyage.name: Scavi Romani di biblioteca salaborsa
voyage.alt: Roman Excavations of the "Stock Exchange" Library
voyage.content: A compact basement-level field of ruins from Bologna's past, from 2nd-century BCE Roman roads and buildings, to a 16th-century CE cistern. Metal walkways take you on a 100-m course over and around the ruins. But this thoughtful display is all the more interesting for its location: under a 19th-century stock exchange hall ("salaborsa"), which has been converted to a 21st-century library. Enjoy this airy, pleasant room

voyage.name: Palazzo dei Banchi
voyage.content: The last palace to be built in Piazza Maggiore. Its current Renaissance-style palace façade dates to the 16th century.

voyage.name: Palazzo d'Accursio
voyage.content: Bologna's city hall, with a very rich collection of Renaissance paintings, sculptures and antique furniture, is a 14th-century palace. Don't miss its enormous main staircase, which was designed to be used by horse drawn carriages.

voyage.name: Palazzo dei Notai
voyage.content: The old seat of the Notary's guild. It was built in 1381 and completely restored in 1908 by Alfonso Rubbiani. Inside there are some frescoes 15th century.

voyage.name: Palazzo dell'Archiginnasio
voyage.hours: Teatro Anatomico & Sala dello Stabat Mater: Mon-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat 10:00-19:00, Sun 10:00-14:00
voyage.content: Once the main building of the University of Bologna, it houses the Biblioteca comunale dell'Archiginnasio (Archiginnasio Municipal Library). The major attractions of the palace which can be visited are the amazing Teatro Anatomico (Anatomical Theatre) and the Sala dello Stabat Mater (Stabat Mater Hall). Both are well worth visiting.

voyage.name: Corte de' Galluzzi
voyage.content: The medieval Torre Galluzzi (Galluzzi Tower) dominates this tiny square.

voyage.name: Via Rizzoli
voyage.content: One of the main streets of Bologna. It is a meeting point and strolling area. It opens up to Piazza di porta Ravegnana, where the two towers rise.

voyage.name: Tombe dei Glossatori
voyage.address: Piazza San Domenico e Piazza Malpighi
voyage.content: Named for the lawyers who used to add glosses (notes) to documents. The tombs, which date from the end of the 13th century, are home to many of Bologna's famous scholars.

voyage.name: Via Santa Caterina
voyage.content: With small houses built in the 16th century.

voyage.name: San Michele in Bosco
voyage.content: Architectural complex comprising the church and adjacent former convent of the Olivetans, with an amazing panoramic view of the city that's great at sunset. Get the number 30 bus if you don't like walking up hills!

voyage.name: Sanctuary of San Luca
voyage.content: Impressive mountain-topped church with a panoramic view which is reachable by a walkway (portico) starting from Porta Saragozza, with over 600 archways - the longest in the world. If you don't want the uphill climb, you can take the San Luca Express tourist train for €13, or the 58 TPER bus (these are small and only run every 30 mins).

voyage.name: Torre degli Asinelli
voyage.content: Closed to the public since October 2023, the tower (built between 1109 and 1119) is 97.20 metres tall (330 feet), with 498 steps and an incline of 1.3 meters (4 feet). Until 2023 you could climb the 498 steps of this tower for spectacular views of the city, but that month it was closed to the public for safety reasons and renovations are expected to take ten years.

voyage.name: Torre dei Garisenda
voyage.content: Torre dei Garisenda is 47 m (162 feet) tall and has a lean of over 3m (10 feet). It was built in the 12th century.

voyage.name: Torre Prendiparte
voyage.content: 60-m tower, the second largest in the city. Presumably it used to be higher than its current height. It's a B＆B and room for events, also hosts shows and presentations.

voyage.name: Torre Azzoguidi
voyage.content: 47 m, built in the 13th century. It's built into the Palazzo del Podestà.

voyage.name: Portico Walk to San Luca
voyage.content: Walk through the historic 666 porticos – the longest portico passage in the world, leaving from the Porta Saragozza at the end of Via Saragozza.

voyage.name: Santuario della Madonna di San Luca
voyage.content: Built in mid-18th century, it offers a panoramic view of the city, although offering only a glimpse of the old historic city. It can be reached by walking along the 666 arches of its unique portico. It has a peculiar layout, being of a round shape. A widely city-known icon, the Madonna di San Luca, is held there.

voyage.name: Finestrella di Via Piella
voyage.content: A little window on the Moline Canal — the Little Venice of Bologna.

voyage.name: Museo Civico Archeologico
voyage.hours: Mon, Wed-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat, Sun and holidays 10:00-19:00
voyage.content: In the Palazzo Galvani – a 14th-century building. This building, an old hospital, houses a comprehensive collection of antiquities from civilizations and cultures including ancient Egypt (mummies and sarcophagi), Iron Age Villanova culture, artifacts from Etruscan Velzna, funerary art, terracotta urns, ancient vases and items from Roman times. Do not miss the bronze Certosa jar, which is over 1,500 years old.

voyage.name: Collezioni Comunali d'Arte
voyage.content: A painting collection of works from various historical periods. Features include works by Giuseppe Maria Crespi (Ritratto del cardinale Lambertini- Portrait of Cardinal Lambertini), Ludovico Carracci (S. Caterina in Carcere – St. Catherine in Prison), and Guido Cagnacci (Cleopatra e Lucrezia), Francesco Hayez (Ruth).

voyage.name: Museo Civico Medievale
voyage.alt: Civic Museum of the Middle Ages
voyage.content: Part of Musei Civici d'Arte Antica.

voyage.name: Museo Davia Bargellini
voyage.hours: Tue–Fri 09:00–13:00, Sat Sun holidays 10:00–18:30, Mon closed
voyage.content: A most curious collection, including religious art of the 1500s, a marionette theatre, an 18th-century gilded carriage, and antique keys and door hardware. Housed in a 17th-century palazzo.

voyage.name: Museo d'Arte Moderna di Bologna
voyage.content: A nice collection of modern art, if you want a break from the more classical pieces that abound in Italy.

voyage.name: Museo Morandi
voyage.content: Opened in 1993, the museum houses most of the works by the Bolognese painter Giorgio Morandi.

voyage.name: International museum and library of music
voyage.alt: Museo Internazionale e Biblioteca della Musica di Bologna
voyage.price: €5, €3 if 65 or older, free if under 18 and on some Th Su
voyage.hours: Museum: Tue–Sun 10:00-18:30, Mon closed; library Tue–Sun 09:30–13:30, Thu also 14:30–16:30
voyage.content: A spectacular collection of music scores, historic instruments, and opera artifacts from 1500 to the early 1900s. There is the first printed score, a 1501 Petrucci. There is the original Clavemusicum Omnitonum of 1606, with 125 keys playing 31 quarter-tones per octave. There is a portrait of Farinelli, perhaps the greatest opera singer of all time. The library was kickstarted in the 1700s by Padre Martini, a Bolognes

voyage.name: Palazzo Poggi
voyage.content: The building houses the headquarters of the University of Bologna. The interior is decorated with frescoes by Pellegrino Tibaldi, on the ground floor is the Hall of Hercules with a statue by Angelo Piò (1730). On the northern side of the Palace is the monumental Aula Magna (1756). Also Palazzo Poggi hosts numerous University Museums. In the University Library of Bologna it has preserved the "Picture Gallery" with ove

voyage.name: Museo della Specola
voyage.hours: guided tours only for groups of 15 people max. Tue-Fri at 10:45, 12:15, 15:00, booking by phone; Sat Sun at 11:00, at 15:00, booking online
voyage.content: At the Specola, an astronomical tower built in the beginning of 18th century over Palazzo Poggi. The material exposed illustrates the evolution of the astronomic instrumentation through the centuries.

voyage.name: Museo Europeo degli Studenti
voyage.content: The Museum of European Students is about the history and culture of university students from the thirteenth to the twentieth century. Closed on Monday; Admission free. Don't miss this when you are interested in student life. It's unique.

voyage.name: Museo Di Fisica
voyage.hours: during renovation works visits are only by guided tours by appointment

voyage.name: Museo di Mineralogia "Luigi Bombicci"
voyage.content: Rocks, precious stones, rare minerals and meteorites

voyage.name: Museo delle Cere anatomiche "Luigi Cattaneo"
voyage.hours: Jun–Aug: Tue-Fri 10:00-13:00, Sat Sun holiday 10:00-18:00, Mon closed; Sep–May: Tue-Fri 9:00-13:00, Sat Sun holiday 10:00-14:00, Mon closed; closed 1 Jan, 1 May, 15 Aug, 24, 25 Dec
voyage.content: If you think Bologna's towers are crooked, then you'll want to see the deformed spines and diseased oddities at this gross-out Wax Museum. Although dedicated to the history of the art of medical anatomical models of the 19th century, the real fun are the conjoined twins and tumor-laden lepers on which showcases the art.

voyage.name: Museo di Antropologia
voyage.content: Bones, and artefacts of prehistoric Italians.

voyage.name: Museo di Anatomia degli Animali Domestici
voyage.alt: Museum of Anatomy of Domestic Animals

voyage.name: Museo di Anatomia Patologica e Teratologia Veterinaria
voyage.alt: Museum of Veterinary Pathology and Teratology
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 09:30-12:30, by appointment only, booking by phone

voyage.name: Orto Botanico ed Erbario
voyage.content: Created in the mid-16th century for medicinal herbs. The Botanical gardens are home to over 5,000 plant species. Some of the highlights include a full-grown sequoia, and a greenhouse for cacti and carnivorous plants.

voyage.name: Palazzo Fava Ghisilieri
voyage.content: 16th-century building decorated by frescoes by Carracci. It hosts temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Palazzo Pepoli Vecchio
voyage.content: The Museum of the history of Bologna is located there.

voyage.name: Oratorio di San Colombano
voyage.content: It hosts the Tagliavini Collection.

voyage.name: Santuario di Santa Maria della Vita
voyage.content: This church contains "The Lamentation", a life-size terracotta group sculpture, Renaissance masterpiece by Niccolò Dell'Arca.

voyage.name: Casa Saraceni
voyage.content: 16th-century building which hosts temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: San Giorgio in Poggiale
voyage.content: A former 16th-century church. It hosts the Biblioteca di Arte e di Storia di San Giorgio in Poggiale (Art and History Library).

voyage.name: Santa Cristina
voyage.content: A former church contains works of Carracci and Guido Reni. It is used for concert performances.

voyage.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna
voyage.content: Containing the city's most important art, it offers an interesting panorama of the Emilian and Venetian painting from the 13th to the 18th century. A must: the works by Giotto, Raffaello, Parmigianino (Madonna col Bambino/Virgin Mary with Baby and the Saints Margaret, Girolamo and Petronio), Perugino, Tiziano and Tintoretto (Visitazione/Visitation and Saints Joseph and Zacharias).

voyage.name: Museo Ebraico
voyage.hours: Sun-Thu 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:00-16:00. Tickets sold until 17:15 (15:15 Fri). Closed Saturdays and on Jewish holidays
voyage.content: Located in the area of the former ghetto, this museum covers the history of Bologna's Jewish population.

voyage.name: Accademia Filarmonica
voyage.content: The Philarmonic Academy of Bologna was established in 1666. Since then it has become a reference point for the city musical life and its fame has spread throughout Europe. Here are preserved the works of many illustrious students, including Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s (1770) and autographed documents by Puccini, Verdi and Beethoven

voyage.name: Galleria d'Arte Moderna “Raccolta Lercaro”
voyage.content: Houses about 2000 works by Italian and foreign artists with special attention to the sculptures by Manzù, Messina, Rodin and Giacometti.

voyage.name: Museo Ducati
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri guided tours at 11:00 and 16:00; Sat 09:00-13:00. Closed during Easter and Christmas holidays and in August
voyage.content: Represents the evolution of the Bolognese motorcycle firm. An exposition of motorcycles, period materials, projects, mechanical components, pictures and videos.

voyage.name: Giardini Margherita
voyage.content: Bologna's main park created in 1875. The chalet converts to a nightclub in the summer evenings.

voyage.name: Giardino della Montagnola
voyage.content: The oldest park in the city. A public park since the 17th century. Much of the current landscaping dates from the early 19th century. The pond in the center of the park was added in 1888.

voyage.name: Villa delle Rose
voyage.content: Donated to the city in 1916, the gardens had been owned by the Cella family. The 18th-century Villa delle Rose, which was the Cella's residence, hosts art exhibitions throughout the year

voyage.name: Villa Spada
voyage.content: On the grounds of the Palazzo Ravone an 18th-century villa, it was opened to the public in 1970.

voyage.name: Villa Guastavillani
voyage.content: Designed and built by Tomasso Martelli in the 16th century.

voyage.name: Parco Cavaioni
voyage.content: A large park featuring meadows, fields, wooded areas, and a lake.

voyage.name: Certosa
voyage.content: Bologna's main cemetery, with beautifully carved tombstones, built over the ruins of an ancient Etrusan necropolis.

voyage.name: Bologna Fiere
voyage.content: An Exhibition Centre near Bologna, that among other things has an International Automobile Exhibition every year.

voyage.name: Estragon
voyage.content: A big ex-industrial hangar, features dj-sets and concerts by international rock bands almost every night.

voyage.name: Livello 57
voyage.content: Now only seldom open. It mainly features raves and techno gigs in an industrial, darkish atmosphere.

voyage.name: TPO
voyage.content: Another occupied location that mostly features experimental music festivals and rock concerts.

voyage.name: XM24
voyage.content: An occupied ex-agricultural market where Punk-hc, rock and electronic concerts are often featured. A very cheap place, great if you don't mind the punk atmosphere. Every Thursday from 17:30, it is an organic market. The place also has plenty of free and self-managed workshops: bike repair (Wednesdays and Sundays from 18:00 to 22:00), a school of Italian (Monday and Tuesday from 18:00 to 21:00), a hacklab (Wednesday 2

voyage.name: VAG61
voyage.content: An historical occupied location that host a wide variety of activities. Every Tuesday from the late afternoon there's an organic market.

voyage.name: The Link
voyage.content: A large, 2-floor club that features mostly avant garde electronic, techno and hip-hop gigs and dj-sets. A little book shop, mainly on "alternative" subjects, can be found inside. By bus: Linea 20, 55 or 35.

voyage.name: Covo Club
voyage.content: "storied and legendary Italian indie-punk venue" (Pitchfork), Covo Club is the most renowned indie rock club, features rock djsets and concerts by a number of interesting international bands. Born in 1980, open on Fridays and Saturdays only, Covo Club has hosted in its life more than 1000 concerts including bands like Franz Ferdinand, The Libertines, Mumford & Sons, The Gossip, Animal Collective, Black Lips, Wild Not

voyage.name: Kindergarten
voyage.content: Next to the "Fiera", is a club that features techno, and sometimes punk and new wave concerts.

voyage.name: Locomotiv
voyage.content: Another indie rock club.

voyage.name: Eataly Bologna
voyage.content: Eataly is a gourmet grocery store associated with Slow movement. It styles itself as a place to "savor high quality traditional Italian food products and beverages along with local produce and artisanal products." Many different products are for sale, including not only produce but cheese, wine, olive oil, and sweets, and there are also a few smaller restaurants. Anyone who enjoys shopping or window-shopping for food

voyage.name: Osteria del Sole
voyage.content: If you feel like picnicking on some of the cold cuts (salumi), cheeses and other fresh foods on display in the delicatessens and market stalls off Piazza Maggiore, then Osteria del Sole at a tiny street could be a perfect venue. This traditional wine-drinkers' osteria (something of a rarity nowadays) invites you to bring along your own food. Popular with locals and travelers alike, it can get full, especially on Satu

voyage.name: Tigellino
voyage.content: Excellent tigelleria. Good ingredients and excellent bread. Characteristic, all kinds of menus including vegetarian. Each tigellini costs €1.70-1.90.

voyage.name: Nectare
voyage.content: A small vegetarian restaurant, choose between prepared dishes. Good healthy bowls and burgers.

voyage.name: Centro Natura
voyage.content: Excellent lunches with the self-service mode, fast and practical, but also beautiful dinners on Friday and Saturday with table service. Vegetarian, organic, good food with large portions, relaxing environment and kind staff.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Altero - via Caprarie
voyage.content: Historic recipe, for over 40 years the same unmistakable flavor. You can enjoy pizza and aperol spritz with a beautiful view of the tower. The pizza is delicious, great variety, always fresh.

voyage.name: Trattori Fantoni
voyage.content: With its checkered red and white table clothes and scribbled menus, Fantoni is much frequented by students. It serves fantastic fish secondi and an excellent ragù. The bread is homemade.

voyage.name: I Matti Della Polenta
voyage.content: An unassuming family-run fast food restaurant with delicious, inexpensive polenta in several variations. Get it griglia (grilled), fritta (fried), or spillata. Choose between several sauces, cheeses, and Nutella toppings. Also tigella (small round bread) and piadina (flatbread sandwich). The friendly owners will be happy to explain, in Italian or English.

voyage.name: Ristorante È Cucina Leopardi
voyage.content: Healthy and satiating cuisine rich in vegetables and fish for just 10-15 EUR: welcome appetizer. Excellent food, seasonally produced and interesting ingredient combinations.

voyage.name: Trattoria Da Vito
voyage.content: Genuine Bolognese fare, from antipasto to dessert, served (occasionally somewhat abruptly) in a down-to-earth trattoria setting popular with locals and visitors alike. Pictures of singer-songwriters such as Lucio Dalla and other local legends performing and soaking up the atmosphere. (Just don't expect anything too ritzy!)

voyage.name: Trattoria da Gianni
voyage.content: Down to earth, home-style cooking.

voyage.name: Mercato di Mezzo
voyage.content: Great place to have lunch or dinner for a good price. There are different local options for food and tables where you can sit down and enjoy your meal. There are many people at all times of day.

voyage.name: Trattoria Del Rosso
voyage.content: Traditional Bolognese dishes seven days a week at very reasonable prices. Owned and operated by chef Stefano Curvucci.

voyage.name: La Salumeria Bruno e Franco
voyage.content: One of Bologna's best delis. Features fresh pasta.

voyage.name: Tamburini
voyage.content: A reasonably priced self-service lunch. Tamburini is renowned locally as one of Bologna's historic delicatessens, and it also provides a good variety of traditional fare at lunchtime for local employees and other visitors. Queues can get long during the peak lunch hour.

voyage.name: Ristorante Teresina
voyage.content: Excellent food. Fish and meat menus, which can change daily, plus a set of traditional Bolognese dishes which are always served.

voyage.name: Ristorante Gusto Chengdu
voyage.content: Delicious and spicy Szechuan Chinese food. Vegetarian options available.

voyage.name: Ristorante Casa Monica
voyage.content: More contemporary stylish dining, excellent and good value.

voyage.name: Ristorante Diana
voyage.content: It is probably the most famous restaurant in the city but now it is a pale shadow of what it once was, though still high on old world atmosphere. Elderly Bolognese, tourists and businessmen dine here. The traditional regional cuisine like Lasagne Bolognese, Tortellini in Brodo and Tagliatelle with Ragu are the best choice here and the service is top notch. The daunting bolito misto is still a favourite and €35 will a

voyage.name: Enoteca Italiana
voyage.content: It has twice been voted best in Italy. Great for a stand up sandwich (Pancetta with Balsamic or a Mortadella Panino) and an excellent glass of the wine of your choice.

voyage.name: Trattoria Mariposa
voyage.content: Down to earth home style cooking.

voyage.name: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele Bologna
voyage.content: Pizza is a Naples thing, but this outpost of one of the best pizzerias of Naples brings their soft, salty heaven to Bologna. The focussed but offers little more than pizza Margherita with normal, double, or no cheese. Pick one, and the crust and sauce will delight.

voyage.name: Trattoria Tony
voyage.content: A down to earth, reasonably-priced place with simple Bolognese food—truly excellent.

voyage.name: Caminetto D'Oro
voyage.content: Good service, good wine list and fine food at a price.

voyage.name: Matusel
voyage.content: A good and tasty meal for as cheap as €10, coffee included. Matusel is renowned for good fish dishes.

voyage.name: Osteria Broccaindosso
voyage.content: Cozy dining room with bolognese traditional dishes, such as tortellini in brodo. Try the mixed vegetables appetiser: a half-dozen bite-sized portions of heaven. The ricotta appetiser melts sweet and soft, like pudding.

voyage.name: Ristorante Cesarina
voyage.content: For good service, good wine list and fine food at a price.

voyage.name: Trattoria Leonida
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 12:30-14:30, 19:30-23:00; Sun closed, except open for lunch on some festival Sundays
voyage.content: This trattoria is hard to fault, with its excellent food and service at fair prices. They promote their vegetarian options. But service can be slow: it could take you a while to get your bill.

voyage.name: L'Antica Trattoria Spiga
voyage.content: A bit hard to find, but make the effort. It has a very good risotto, and wonderful traditional Cucina Bolognese. If you are blessed to visit on a Wednesday, don't miss out on the day's special, a platter with crescente bread served with cold cured meats and cheeses for savoury, and nutella and jams for dessert. Be prepared to know a little Italian.

voyage.name: Trattoria Meloncello
voyage.hours: Daily 12:30–15:00, 19:30–23:00 (kitchen stops 00:30 earlier than closing time)
voyage.content: Down to earth home style cooking.

voyage.name: L'Antica Osteria Romagnola
voyage.content: It is very pretty and does good food but refuse the abundant (and expensive) antipasto or have that and just one other course.

voyage.name: Ristorante Al Pappagallo
voyage.price: €60-90 for first and second courses, or tasting menu (Nov 2019)
voyage.content: It was a famous haunt of the stars during the 1960s and '70s and still attracts an exclusive clientele. Its mix of traditional Bolognese fare and nouvelle cuisine gives the Diana a run for its money. Many other restaurants offer the same food for a lot less, but you get a lot of space between the tables here and the historic building is impressive if that is what you want. They offer both meat-based and vegetarian ta

voyage.name: Grom
voyage.content: Consistently superb gelato, from the local outpost of an Italian chain. Try the pistachio, and the almond "granita".

voyage.name: Caffè Terzi
voyage.content: Features single estate coffees.

voyage.name: Caffè Zanarini
voyage.content: Best terrace in town. Stylish waiters serve quality food. A 0.75 l bottle San Pellegrino costs €2.50. Good value for your money.

voyage.name: Gamberini
voyage.hours: Closed Thu afternoon and Sun evenings.
voyage.content: Some of the finest appetizers in town; great pastries (paste) too.

voyage.name: Pasticceria Antica Bologna
voyage.content: A smart but not particularly expensive bar and patisserie which also does an excellent pre-dinner aperitivo. Good coffee.

voyage.name: Il Gelatauro
voyage.hours: Summer Tue–Thu 08:30–22:30; Fri Sat 08:30–23:30; Sun 09:00–20:30; Mon closed; closed August; winter hours differ
voyage.content: Superb pistachio and chocolate gelato, and many unique gelato flavors, like Parmigiano with Pears, or Fig and Almond, or Watermelon and Jasmine. Considered one of the best gelaterie in all Italy.

voyage.name: Stefino
voyage.content: A contender for the title of Bologna's Best Gelato. Largely organic. Try the wonderful pistachio, and the almond "granita".

voyage.name: Cremeria Cavour
voyage.content: This new arrival on the gelato scene is giving everyone else a run for their money with many excellent flavor combinations.

voyage.name: La Sorbetteria Castiglione
voyage.content: Excellent gelato (ice cream). Once upon a time, the best in town, but there are others are in the running. There is a second branch at Via Saragozza, 83.

voyage.name: Ai Vini Scelti
voyage.content: A good enoteca (winery), just outside the center in Via Andrea Costa and only a few moments from Via Pratello, is considered one of the best in Bologna, though there are many others in the center, providing everything from a quick aperitivo to proper wine-tasting. Another good winery is "Vini d'Italia" in Emilia Levante street (Viale Lenin corner), which is one of the oldest on in the city.

voyage.name: Collegio Universitario S. Tommaso d'Aquino a Bologna
voyage.price: €50 for 1 person; parking is €10 (extremely hard to find a parking place on the nearby streets) but you're not allowed to enter the city center, including the area where hotel is located, by car before 20:00.
voyage.content: A part of San Tommaso's college but available for booking to everyone. Good location, cheap, free and high-speed Wi-Fi. Reception is not 24 hours! It is closed from 01:00-07:00 (08:00 during weekends), you will not be able to enter the hotel after 01:00 - it is possible to extend it for €20-30 till 02:00-03:00 respectively, but only in advance.

voyage.name: Il Nosadillo
voyage.content: Beds in shared rooms with a private locker for each guest, access to kitchen & public computer, breakfast, free WiFi and map of the city. Has 1 mixed 4 bed dorm and 1 mixed 5 bed dorm. Two bathrooms. In the heart of historical city center. Easy access to public transport.

voyage.name: Amadeus Hotel
voyage.content: The Amadeus Hotel is near the Bologna airport, in the city's nearest suburban area. 99 rooms. About 15 minutes by car or bus from the central station.

voyage.name: B&B Bologna nel Cuore
voyage.content: Two bedrooms and two studios. An intimate and stylish bed & breakfast located in an ancient building in the historic center of Bologna.

voyage.name: Beatrice B&B Bologna
voyage.content: Three rooms each with a private bathroom. B&B is in an elegant apartment attic with elevator in the centre of Bologna, next to the railway station, university, and all bus lines. A rich breakfast is served by friendly owners.

voyage.name: Hotel Fiera
voyage.price: Prices vary widely based on date: €38-240
voyage.content: A very nice hotel in the Merchant district with 99 rooms. If you are lucky enough to get a room with a balcony, you will be rewarded with an outstanding view of the Apennines in the distance. Friendly staff, and a very nice little restaurant. Breakfast here is lovely. If you want a place on the outskirts from which to plan your stay, you could do much worse, but at a significant distance from the center, public trans

voyage.name: Hotel HC3 Bologna
voyage.price: Summer €55-155, fall €70-200; winter €60-130. Internet discounts available
voyage.content: Located near the City Fair and a few minutes from downtown. 37 rooms, four stars. Free wi-fi internet connection, modern gym and a comfortable meeting room. Peculiar to the hotel is courtesy coffee around the clock available for free on every floor.

voyage.name: Hotel Imperial
voyage.content: Hotel with meeting rooms, wellness center and gym, a good choice for business travelers or for a relaxing holiday. Located near a bus no.25 stop, which takes you straight to the railway station. 49 rooms, three stars.

voyage.name: Mercure Bologna Centro
voyage.content: The Mercure is a rather conspicuously aged former Sofitel, with inoperative trouser presses and bathrooms straight out of the early 1980s. It remains very popular, however, due to its location right in front of the Bologna Centrale railway station.

voyage.name: NH Bologna de la Gare
voyage.content: Within a few steps of Bologna Centrale and right at the grand stairs of Parco Montagnola. The more expensive rooms have been refitted to current NH standards, the cheapest ones retain their Italiante looks and fixtures from the times this used to be a Jolly Hotel.

voyage.name: NH Bologna Villanova
voyage.address: Via Villanova, 29/8. 40055 Villanova di Castenaso. Bologna
voyage.content: The other NH in Bologna is a modern hotel is located within a commercial estate to the west of the city, with limited access by public transportation. Relatively attractive prices offset its remote location. It is best suited for business travellers with interest in the immediate vicinity or those arriving by car.

voyage.name: Hotel Porta San Mamolo
voyage.content: A much-loved small hotel, lauded for its lovely staff, comfortable and prettily decorated rooms, and central but quiet location. 43 rooms, three stars.

voyage.name: Hotel University Bologna
voyage.content: Close to the “Universitá degli Studi”. 22 rooms, three stars. A breakfast buffet is inclusive in the price.

voyage.name: Residence alle Scuole
voyage.content: Relaxing country hotel near Bologna. All rooms have satellite TV, telephone, air conditioning, private bath and free internet connection. 14 rooms, three stars.

voyage.name: Residence Porta Saragozza
voyage.content: Elegant suite and apartments comfortably furnished in every detail, placed in quiet Bologna zone. Close to public transport and shops. Apartments to rent in Bologna and Pontecchio Marconi Sasso Marconi.

voyage.name: Residenza Ariosto
voyage.content: Elegant residence in the center of Bologna. Close to public transport, shops, university and hospital.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Baglioni
voyage.content: A grand large fairly elegant hotel

voyage.name: I Portici Hotel Bologna
voyage.content: A luxury property in the heart of town, walking distance from the main train station, the city centre shopping area and nearby to Bologna fair exposition area. Four stars.

voyage.name: Il Convento dei Fiori di Seta
voyage.content: A stylish little hotel that has been fitted into a small restored church. Four stars.

voyage.name: Relais Villa Valfiore
voyage.address: Via Imelda Lambertini 20, San Lazzaro di Savena
voyage.content: In a park of century-old trees in an enchanting corner of the hills in the Municipality of San Lazzaro di Savena, just a few kilometres from Bologna.
